approved_now_count.description: Readers approvable now on a time-boxed grant.

binding_policy_clause.description: The operative clause cited to refuse the out-of-scope and conflicting asks.

business_need_date.description: Documented business or clinical control date that the decision must protect (ISO date).

controlled_item_or_record.description: Immutable item, lot set, or transaction record in scope.

cost_of_delay_usd.description: Incremental cost of the expedited-attestation escalation path.

decision_timing_status.description: ON_TIME when the selected outcome is on or before the control date; otherwise LATE.

duplicate_request_count.description: Read requests consolidated to an earlier open request.

escalation_approval_required.description: Use 1 when an alternative is outside current authority and would need a separate approval; otherwise 0.

exception_required_count.description: Readers blocked on a missing data-handling attestation.

excluded_quantity.description: read requests blocked on a missing attestation, a duplicate, or a segregation-of-duties conflict

observed_quantity.description: Gross observed quantity before applying the control for today's confidential warehouse read batch.

outcome_vs_control_days.description: Selected outcome date minus the documented control date; positive means late.

quantity_unit.description: Unit of measure for every controlled quantity: REQUEST.

recommended_incremental_cost_usd.description: Documented incremental spend of the selected option in USD; zero when spend is not a decision driver.

facts.rubric: Located RES-WH-READ using immutable identifiers and preserved effective standard v5: resource code warehouse-read resolves to RES-WH-READ; the warehouse-write role (RES-WH-WRITE) is a different resource owned by the warehouse data owner.
facts.statement: AGR-0002: resource code warehouse-read resolves to RES-WH-READ; the warehouse-write role (RES-WH-WRITE) is a different resource owned by the warehouse data owner; the effective standard is v5.

facts.rubric: Applied the operative clause and the request batch to establish 6 REQUEST for read requests that need a coverage decision after removing the duplicate and the refusal (approve-now plus exception-eligible), with control date 2026-05-20.
facts.statement: The operative clause and the request batch establish read requests that need a coverage decision after removing the duplicate and the refusal (approve-now plus exception-eligible) = 6 REQUEST: eight pending read requests, of which one is a duplicate and one a refused conflict, leave six coverage decisions and a group grant covering the four eligible now. The control date is 2026-05-20 (the analytics squad's onboarding milestone is 2026-05-20 and the readers must be provisioned before it).

facts.rubric: Reconciled 8 observed less 4 excluded to 4 eligible REQUEST for read requests approvable now on a time-boxed grant under the v5 standard.
facts.statement: four readers hold the current DATA-HANDLING-2026 attestation; one contractor is missing it and one request bundles an out-of-scope write ask; eligibility requires netting the blocked and duplicate requests rather than trusting the raw queue.

facts.rubric: Used the independently confirmed 2026-05-14 expedited screening readiness for expedite_attestation_via_tier2, then separately derived its 2026-05-14 operating outcome under the v5 confidential clause and the signed approval scope instead of treating a vendor promise as authorization or a completion date.
facts.statement: Attesta's confirmed standard and expedited data-handling clearance dates on RQ-52001: Attesta RQ-52001 confirms standard clearance 2026-05-15 and expedited 2026-05-13 (+USD 180); eligibility is the next business day; a vendor confirmation alone proves neither eligibility nor approval.

facts.rubric: Applied approver review windows that do not displace protected blocks to derive the three option outcomes without using protected or blocked review windows.
facts.statement: approver review windows that do not displace protected blocks: the first free review window on or after 2026-05-18 is APR-2 AM on 2026-05-18; protected and blocked review windows cannot be displaced.

facts.rubric: Applied AP-AG-0102 only to grant_read_cohort and RES-WH-READ; kept expedite_attestation_via_tier2 outside current authority.
facts.statement: AP-AG-0102 covers a read grant for up to 4 requests; write access and the expedite fee are out of scope. The approval does not select an option in advance and does not authorize expedite_attestation_via_tier2.

facts.rubric: Compared all three alternatives and selected grant_read_cohort: it is the best currently authorized disposition that satisfies the v5 confidential clause and the signed approval scope.
facts.statement: the onboarding milestone is 2026-05-20 and the eligible readers must be on before it; a faster or broader disposition has value only if it stays inside the v5 confidential clause and the signed approval scope.

options.consequence: grant read cohort provisions the 4 attested readers on a 60-day time-boxed read grant and routes the 2 blocked readers to standard data-handling attestation, clearing on the 2026-05-18 review window, at no incremental cost.
options.label: grant_read_cohort: outcome 2026-05-18, incremental cost USD 0, SUPPORTED_AND_APPROVED

options.consequence: expedite attestation via tier-2 clears the blocked readers earlier for USD 180, but the expedite fee and the tier-2 exception need the risk committee, which AP-AG-0102 does not carry.
options.label: expedite_attestation_via_tier2: outcome 2026-05-14, incremental cost USD 180, SEPARATE_APPROVAL_OR_POLICY_EXCEPTION_REQUIRED

options.consequence: grant bundled write would add the requested write role to the read grant, but write access is out of this approval's scope and the vendor-master reader is a segregation-of-duties conflict, so the evidence does not support it.
options.label: grant_bundled_write: outcome 2026-05-12, incremental cost USD 0, FAILS_CURRENT_CONTROL
